Load employees\n    employees = {}\n    with open('/app/dataset/employees.csv') as f:\n        reader = csv.DictReader(f)\n        for row in reader:\n            pesel = row['PESEL'].strip()\n            employees[pesel] = {\n                'first_name': row['first_name'].strip(),\n                'middle_name': row['middle_name'].strip(),\n                'last_name': row['last_name'].strip(),\n                'gender': row['gender'].strip(),\n                'date_of_birth': row['date_of_birth'].strip(),\n                'position': row['position'].strip(),\n                'hire_date': row['hire_date'].strip(),\n                'hourly_rate': float(row['hourly_rate'].strip()),\n            }\n    \n    # Load tasks\n    tasks = {}\n    with open('/app/dataset/tasks.csv') as f:\n        reader = csv.DictReader(f)\n        for row in reader:\n            task_id = int(row['task_id'].strip())\n            tasks[task_id] = {\n                'description': row['description'].strip(),\n                'difficulty': row['difficulty'].strip(),\n                'pay_per_completion': float(row['pay_per_completion'].strip()),\n                'category': row['category'].strip(),\n            }\n    \n    # Load timesheet\n    timesheet_entries = []\n    with open('/app/dataset/timesheet.csv') as f:\n        reader = csv.DictReader(f)\n        for row in reader:\n            entry = {\n                'id': int(row['id'].strip()),\n                'date_str': row['date'].strip(),\n                'hours_worked': float(row['hours_worked'].strip()),\n                'performed_tasks_str': row['performed_tasks'].strip(),\n                'employee_id': row['employee_id'].strip(),\n                'facility_id': row['facility_id'].strip(),\n                'salary_amount': float(row['salary_amount'].strip()),\n                'bonus': float(row['bonus'].strip()),\n            }\n            timesheet_entries.append(entry)\n    \n    # Parse and validate dates\n    # Correct invalid dates\n    def parse_date(date_str):\n        try:\n            return datetime.strptime(date_str, '%Y-%m-%d').date()\n        except ValueError:\n            # Try to fix - e.g., April 31 -> April 30, June 31 -> June 30\n            parts = date_str.split('-')\n            year, month = int(parts[0]), int(parts[1])\n            day = int(parts[2])\n            # Determine max days in month\n            if month == 2:\n                # Check leap year\n                if (year % 4 == 0 and year % 100 != 0) or (year % 400 == 0):\n                    max_day = 29\n                else:\n                    max_day = 28\n            elif month in [4, 6, 9, 11]:\n                max_day = 30\n            else:\n                max_day = 31\n            if day > max_day:\n                day = max_day\n            return date(year, month, day)\n    \n    def validate_pesel(pesel_str):\n        \"\"\"Validate PESEL checksum and return True if valid.\"\"\"\n        if not re.match(r'^\\d{11}$', pesel_str):\n            return False\n        weights = [1, 3, 7, 9, 1, 3, 7, 9, 1, 3]\n        digits = [int(d) for d in pesel_str[:10]]\n        checksum = sum(w * d for w, d in zip(weights, digits)) % 10\n        checksum = (10 - checksum) % 10\n        return checksum == int(pesel_str[10])\n    \n    def levenshtein(s1, s2):\n        if len(s1) < len(s2):\n            return levenshtein(s2, s1)\n        if len(s2) == 0:\n            return len(s1)\n        prev_row = range(len(s2) + 1)\n        for i, c1 in enumerate(s1):\n            curr_row = [i + 1]\n            for j, c2 in enumerate(s2):\n                insertions = prev_row[j + 1] + 1\n                deletions = curr_row[j] + 1\n                substitutions = prev_row[j] + (c1 != c2)\n                curr_row.append(min(insertions, deletions, substitutions))\n            prev_row = curr_row\n        return prev_row[-1]\n    \n    def correct_pesel(pesel_str):\n        \"\"\"Try to correct invalid PESEL to known one.\"\"\"\n        if pesel_str in employees:\n            return pesel_str\n        # Find closest match by Levenshtein distance\n        best_match = None\n        best_dist = float('inf')\n        for emp_pesel in employees:\n            dist = levenshtein(pesel_str, emp_pesel)\n            if dist < best_dist:\n                best_dist = dist\n                best_match = emp_pesel\n        if best_dist <= 2:\n            return best_match\n        return None\n    \n    # Parse task lists, handle malformed brackets\n    def parse_task_list(task_str):\n        # Remove brackets and quotes\n        task_str = task_str.strip()\n        # Handle various malformed formats\n        # Remove leading [ and trailing ] if present\n        # Handle cases like [244, 900, 961\" or 146, 956, 961]\n        task_str = task_str.replace('[', '').replace(']', '').replace('\"', '').replace(\"'\", \"\")\n        if not task_str:\n            return []\n        parts = [p.strip() for p in task_str.split(',')]\n        task_ids = []\n        for p in parts:\n            if p:\n                try:\n                    task_ids.append(int(p))\n                except ValueError:\n                    pass\n        # Filter to valid task IDs only\n        valid_tasks = [tid for tid in task_ids if tid in tasks]\n        return valid_tasks\n    \n    # Process entries\n    # Group by (pesel, year, month)\n    salary_by_pesel_month = defaultdict(float)\n    \n    for entry in timesheet_entries:\n        # Parse date\n        d = parse_date(entry['date_str'])\n        \n        # Validate/correct PESEL\n        pesel = correct_pesel(entry['employee_id'])\n        if pesel is None:\n            continue  # Skip entries with uncorrectable PESEL\n        \n        hourly_rate = employees[pesel]['hourly_rate']\n        hours = entry['hours_worked']\n        if hours < 0:\n            continue\n        \n        # Parse tasks and compute bonus\n        valid_tasks = parse_task_list(entry['performed_tasks_str'])\n        \n        # Compute bonus from valid tasks\n        computed_bonus = sum(tasks[tid]['pay_per_completion'] for tid in valid_tasks)\n        \n        # Also check the bonus column for consistency\n        # Use the higher of computed bonus or provided bonus (if positive)?\n        # Actually, the problem says \"bonuses earned for completed tasks\" so we should use \n        # the computed bonus from tasks.\n        \n        # But wait - what if the bonus column contains additional bonus that's not from tasks?\n        # Let me just use computed_bonus for now.\n        \n        # Actually, on second thought, re-reading the problem:\n        # \"total hours worked in the month × hourly rate) + any bonuses earned for completed tasks\"\n        # The bonus is from tasks. So use computed bonus.\n        \n        bonus = computed_bonus\n        \n        # Monthly salary for this entry\n        monthly_salary = hours * hourly_rate + bonus\n        \n        # Key by (pesel, year, month)\n        key = (pesel, d.year, d.month)\n        salary_by_pesel_month[key] += monthly_salary\n    \n    # Group by PESEL and sort by month\n    result = defaultdict(list)\n    for (pesel, year, month), total in salary_by_pesel_month.items():\n        rounded = round(total)\n        result[pesel].append((year, month, rounded))\n    \n    # Sort by month and format\n    final_result = {}\n    for pesel in sorted(result.keys()):\n        entries = sorted(result[pesel], key=lambda x: (x[0], x[1]))\n        final_result[pesel] = [e[2] for e in entries]\n    \n    return final_result\n```\n\nWait, I need to also think about the billing period more carefully. \n\n\"For each month, the billing period for all employees starts on the same day of the week inherited from the dataset's earliest record.\"\n\nI think maybe this determines the boundary between months.
